name: M5Stack Unit PIR motion sensor
description: Grove-connector passive-infrared motion sensor from M5Stack: a Nanyang Senba AS312 digital PIR detector with an HT7533 3.3 V regulator, so OUT goes high (about 3.3 V, through 1 kOhm) for about 2 s whenever a warm body moves within about 5 m in a cone under 100 degrees, re-triggering while motion continues. Sensitivity and hold time are fixed. Draws under 60 uA from the 5 V Grove supply. Sold as: M5Stack Unit PIR (SKU U004), white 32 x 24 mm unit with HY2.0-4P Grove socket OUT, NC, 5V, GND.
eli5: A heat-motion detector on a Grove cable: when a person or animal moves in front of it, it sets its output pin high for about two seconds.

pins.name: OUT
pins.description: Motion output (Grove pin 1, white wire): AS312 REL through a 1 kOhm resistor, about 3.3 V for ~2 s per trigger, 0 V otherwise. Safe for 3.3 V GPIOs.

pins.name: 5V
pins.description: Supply (Grove pin 3, red wire): 5 V into the HT7533 3.3 V regulator.

buildNotes: Grove connector order (M5Stack schematic J1): pin 1 OUT (white), pin 2 NC (yellow), pin 3 5V (red), pin 4 GND (black). The unit has a HY2.0-4P Grove socket, not header pins: use a Grove-to-female-jumper cable to reach the breadboard.
Power it from 5 V (ESP32 5V/VIN, Pico VBUS). The on-board HT7533 makes 3.3 V for the AS312, so OUT is about 3.3 V and connects straight to a GPIO.
OUT is active high: 1 for about 2 s (AS312 TOH 2.3 s) after motion, re-triggered while motion continues, then 0 with a ~2.3 s lock time. Timing and sensitivity cannot be adjusted.
On an M5Stack Core use Port B (white wire = GPIO36); Port A is the I2C port and also works as plain GPIO.
Give it up to a minute after power-up to settle. It senses moving warm bodies, not still ones, and cannot see through glass.

driver.code:
# M5Stack Unit PIR (U004), MicroPython driver.
# The unit carries a Nanyang Senba AS312 digital PIR detector (amplifier, filter and
# decision logic inside the can) powered from an HT7533 3.3 V LDO fed by the Grove 5 V.
# The AS312 REL output is push-pull from its 3.3 V rail (VOH > VDD - 1 V, VOL < 1 V at
# 10 mA) and reaches the Grove OUT pin (white wire) through a 1 kOhm series resistor:
#   HIGH (about 3.3 V) for ~2.3 s (TOH) after motion, re-triggering while motion continues
#   LOW  (0 V) otherwise; after falling it ignores motion for ~2.3 s (lock time TOL).
# Safe for 3.3 V GPIOs even though the unit is powered from 5 V. No pull-up/down needed.
# Allow up to a minute after power-up for the detector to settle.
from machine import Pin


class M5PIR:
    def __init__(self, out_pin):
        self.pin = Pin(out_pin, Pin.IN) if isinstance(out_pin, int) else out_pin

    def motion(self):
        """True while the unit reports motion (OUT high)."""
        return self.pin.value() == 1

    def on_change(self, handler):
        """Call handler(motion: bool) on every edge of OUT. Pass None to stop."""
        if handler is None:
            self.pin.irq(handler=None)
            return
        self.pin.irq(trigger=Pin.IRQ_RISING | Pin.IRQ_FALLING,
                     handler=lambda p: handler(p.value() == 1))

example.code:
from m5_pir import M5PIR
import time

pir = M5PIR({OUT})
while True:
    print('MOTION=%d' % pir.motion())
    time.sleep(0.5)
